claims.text: Applying an ultrathin conformal ceria overcoat by ALD to Pt nanoparticles on high-surface-area alumina will improve catalytic activity.
The ceria overcoat will improve catalyst durability.
The ceria overcoat will permit reduced PGM consumption.
The baseline is a conventional automotive exhaust catalyst consisting of Pt nanoparticles dispersed on high-surface-area gamma-alumina.
The proposed ceria overcoat thickness is 1–2 nm.
Low-temperature ALD will provide conformal ceria coverage.
The ceria overcoat will prevent Pt nanoparticle agglomeration and sintering.
The ceria overcoat will maintain catalytically active interfacial sites.
Physical stabilization by the overcoat will limit Pt nanoparticle growth during high-temperature exposure.
Ceria may provide oxygen-storage and oxygen-release functionality.
Synergy at the ceria–Pt interface may enhance exhaust-relevant redox reactions.
Enhanced redox reactions and Pt stabilization will improve catalytic activity even at reduced PGM loading.
Compared with uncoated Pt/alumina, coated Pt/alumina will retain greater catalytic activity after thermal aging.
Reduced-Pt coated catalysts will perform without compromising performance relative to the conventional uncoated baseline.
The expected benefits depend on maintaining the overcoat near an optimal thickness of 1–2 nm.
An excessively thick ceria overcoat may reduce activity by impeding reactant access.
The expected benefits should persist during exhaust-like temperature cycling up to 800°C in oxidizing gas containing O2, CO, NOx, and hydrocarbons.
Prior studies in other catalyst systems suggest that ALD overcoats improve catalyst stability.
